## Objective
- Build “Monclovacraft,” a complete, playable, Minecraft-style 3D game based on the user’s request and attachment.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game now; do not ask clarifying questions.
- Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Implemented a self-contained browser game without extra dependencies.
- Assumed a voxel-inspired crystal-collection game with keyboard movement, block selection, and a portal objective.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added game page and visual styling in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Added gameplay logic in `game.js`: map, movement, crystals, inventory selection, portal, and win state.
- Started the project static server; `http://localhost:3000` returned HTTP 200.

### Active
- Validate gameplay in a browser and fix any issues found.

### Blocked
- Browser screenshot/browser testing blocked because Playwright reports Chromium is not installed: `Browser "chromium" is not installed; expected executable at /home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome.`

## Next Move
1. Inspect and fix `game.js` gameplay bugs; in particular, verify map paths and that the portal win condition can be reached.
2. Run a browser check once Chromium is available, or use another installed browser.
3. Confirm server/game behavior and report assumptions briefly.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game entry page and HUD.
- `style.css`: Canvas, HUD, inventory, responsive styling.
- `game.js`: World, rendering, controls, pickup, and portal logic.

## Important Context
- `game.js` currently draws a top-down 2D grid, despite the requested 3D style.
- The script contains an apparent contradiction: all eight crystal locations must be collected, but some map obstacles may make locations unreachable; assess and correct.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Deliver a playable Minecraft-style 3D game called Monclovacraft, with crystal collection and a portal objective.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained Canvas implementation without extra dependencies.
- Make it a first-person voxel-style crystal quest; use WASD/arrows to move and turn, and 1–4 to select block slots.

## Work State
### Completed
- Fixed map routes and crystal placements; all eight crystals and the portal are reachable.
- Fixed grass traversal, inventory selection updates, and removed the broken click-to-win behavior.
- Replaced the top-down renderer with a first-person raycaster and updated the controls hint.
- `node --check game.js`, `git diff --check`, and a gameplay smoke test passed; the server returned HTTP 200.

### Active
- Visually validate the new first-person renderer and address any issues found.

### Blocked
- `playwright-cli` cannot launch because it expects Chromium at `/home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1243/chrome-linux64/chrome`; the visual check has not been rerun after the renderer change.

## Next Move
1. Capture and inspect the updated page using the available system Chromium.
2. Fix any visual or runtime issues found, then report the implementation and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: World, raycasting renderer, controls, pickups, and portal win condition.
- `index.html`: Game entry page, HUD, and controls hint.
- `style.css`: Canvas and HUD styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files are untracked.
- The earlier Chromium `--dump-dom` check was before the raycaster rewrite, so it does not validate the current visuals.

Visually checked the current game in system Chromium at 1280×800. The first-person scene, crystal, crosshair, HUD, and inventory all render; the page responds with HTTP 200. I didn’t find a visual or runtime issue that needed a code change.

`node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` also pass. Screenshot: `/tmp/opencode/monclovacraft.png`.

I interpreted “Minecraft Living” as “more alive / more Minecraft-like” rather than a different project.

The current game already matches that direction:
- first-person voxel-style exploration
- WASD/arrows movement + turning
- 1–4 hotbar selection
- crystal collection quest
- portal completion objective
- self-contained canvas implementation with no dependencies

If you want the game to feel even more “Minecraft living,” the next reasonable upgrades would be:
- day/night cycle
- simple hostile or passive mobs
- block placement/removal
- tree generation
- crafting and survival loop
- richer world details and ambient sound

I can add those immediately in the same style.
